Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 94, verses 1–3:

And he heard a reciter reciting: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you? (1) And We removed from you your burden (2)﴾

So he said: God expanded the breast of His Messenger (ﷺ) to the fullest expansion, removed his burden entirely, and raised his remembrance completely.

He also granted his followers a share of that, for every one who is followed has a portion and share of the good and evil of his followers' share in what he has, according to the degree of their following of him.

So the people most closely following His Messenger (ﷺ) are the most expanded in breast, the lightest in burden, and the highest in remembrance. Whenever his following grows stronger in knowledge, action, state, and striving (jihad), these three things grow stronger, until the one who has them becomes the most expanded in breast and the highest in remembrance among the worlds.

As for the removal of his burden, how would it not be removed from him, when those in the heavens and the earth, and the beasts of land and sea, seek forgiveness for him?

These three matters are mutually linked, just as their opposites are linked. Sins and transgressions constrict and tighten the breast, and lower and diminish remembrance. Likewise, constriction of the breast lowers remembrance and brings about burdens. No one falls into sins and burdens except through the constriction of his breast and his lack of expansion. The more the breast tightens, the more it calls to sins and burdens, because one who commits them only intends by them to expand his breast and to relieve what he is in of constriction and distress. Otherwise, if it were expanded by monotheism (tawhid), faith, love of God, and knowing Him, and it expanded through that, he would have no need to expand it through burdens. For this reason, most who fall into what is forbidden are only seeking through it to repel from themselves the worry, grief, and constriction within them. Often his desire and will cool, yet he still eagerly returns to it, seeking a cure by his own claim, as the master of debauchery Abu Nuwas made clear when he said:

*And a cup I drank for its pleasure,*
*And another I took as a cure from it.*

So when the servant bears burdens, this necessarily brings upon him constriction of the breast and lowering of remembrance; then lowering of remembrance necessitates constriction of the breast for him. The one who turns away from obedience to God and His Messenger therefore never ceases to oscillate between these three stations, just as the one who obeys God and His Messenger, whose heart has been touched by the spirit of tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) and its purification (tajrid), love of God and His Messenger, and compliance with His command, continues to move between those three stations.

When the back is weighed down with burdens, it prevents the heart from journeying to God and the limbs from rising to obey Him. How can one who is weighed down by a load on his back cross the distance of a journey?

And how can a heart that burdens have weighed down rise toward God?

If his burdens were removed from him, it would rise and fly with longing for its Lord, and his hardship would turn into ease. For constriction of the breast, bearing of burdens, and lowering of remembrance are among the greatest hardships, and with them is an ease that turns him toward Him: namely, the purification of tawhid and the purification of obedience through following the Messenger.

These are the two foundations with which the surah concludes, when He says: ﴿So when you are free, toil (7), and to your Lord turn eagerly (8)﴾

So "toil" (al-nasb) means devoting oneself to worship and obedience, and "turning eagerly to God alone" means purifying His oneness. Whenever one establishes these two foundations, he attains from the expansion of the breast, the removal of the burden, and the raising of remembrance according to what he has established, and his hardship is replaced with ease.

(Benefit)

The splitting of the Prophet's breast (ﷺ), in which his heart was purified and filled with faith and wisdom, is evidence that the seat of intellect is the heart, and that it is connected to the brain.

Some jurists (fuqaha) used as evidence the washing of the Prophet's heart (ﷺ) in a golden basin to permit adorning the mushafs (Qur'an copies) and the mosques with gold.

But this is far-fetched, for that happened before prophethood, and it was not of worldly gold. It was a dignity with which he was honored by the action of the angels by God's command, and they are not included under the obligations of humans.

[Section: The Station of the Murad (the one who is willed)]

[The Reality of the Murad]

Among the stations of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" is the station of the murad (the one willed by God).

Abu Ali al-Daqqaq said: The murid bears (the burden), and the murad is carried. Musa (ﷺ) was a murid when he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾ [Ta-Ha: 25]

And our Prophet (ﷺ) was a murad when it was said to him: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1]

Al-Junayd was asked about the murid and the murad.

He said: The murid's management is taken up by knowledge; the murad's care is taken up by the Truth. Because the murid travels, and the murad flies.

So when does the traveler catch up with the flier?

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Allah raised his remembrance for him, so He is never mentioned except that he is mentioned along with Him."

In this there is a point that requires consideration, because the mention of him ﷺ alongside the mention of his Lord is itself the testimony to his prophethood, once one testifies to the Oneness of the One who sent him.

This is indeed obligatory in the khutbah beyond any doubt; rather, it is its greatest pillar.

Abu Dawud, Ahmad and others have related from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Every khutbah in which there is no tashahhud is like the amputated hand."

(Its isnad is strong.)

Al-yad al-judhma' is the cut-off hand.

Whoever makes sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ obligatory in the khutbah but not the tashahhud, his statement is extremely weak.

Yunus related from Shayban, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, that he said: "Allah raised his remembrance in this world and the Hereafter. So there is no preacher, no one who recites the tashahhud, and no one who prays, except that he begins with: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Abd ibn Humayd said: Amr ibn Awn informed me, from Hushaym, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, that he said: "When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with me, and no khutbah or marriage is valid without mention of you."

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, that he said: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with me, and no khutbah or marriage is valid without mention of you."

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, that he said: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with me, [namely] in the adhan: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

(Its isnad is sahih.)

This, then, is the meaning of the verse. How could the tashahhud, which is the bond of Islam, not be obligatory in the khutbah, when it is its best words, and when sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ is obligatory within it?

(Benefit)

The defined (al-ma'rif) noun, even if it is mentioned repeatedly and its wording is the same, is one thing; this is unlike the indefinite (al-munakkar).

Whoever understands this understands the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Hardship will not overcome two eases" (mursal, but it has chains of transmission that strengthen it).

For he (ﷺ) was pointing to the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease.﴾

Thus, "hardship" (al-'usr), though it is repeated twice, is repeated with the definite form, so it is one; and "ease" (al-yusr) is repeated with the indefinite form, so it is two eases.

Hence the hardship is enclosed between two eases: an ease before it and an ease after it, so hardship will not overcome two eases.

He said in (Shifa' al-'Alil):

And "hardship will not overcome two eases."

This is because Mercy overcame Wrath, pardon preceded punishment, blessing preceded trial, and goodness belongs to the attributes and the actions, while evil belongs to the objects of action and not to the actions themselves.

So His attributes are all perfection, and His actions are all good. For the pain of a living creature does not leave it without well-being that is greater than that pain, or a preparation for strength, health and perfection, or a compensation to which that pain bears no relation in any way.

So the sum of all the pains of this world, in relation to the pleasures and goods of the Hereafter, is far less than the proportion of a speck of dust to the mountains of this world.

And likewise, all the pleasures of this world, in relation to the pains of the Hereafter.

Allah, glorified is He, did not create pains and pleasures in vain, nor did He ordain them without purpose.

And from the perfection of His power and wisdom is that He made each of them yield the other.

Moreover, the necessary consequences of creation cannot be removed, just as poverty, need and deficiency cannot be removed from the created being; the created being is only poor, needy, deficient in knowledge and power. Had a human being and other animals not hungered, thirsted or suffered in this world of generation and corruption, they would not be animals, and this abode would be a dwelling of absolute, perfect permanence and pleasure. But Allah did not make it so; rather He made it an abode in which its pain is mixed with its pleasure, its joy with its sorrows and griefs, and its health with its sickness, by His consummate wisdom.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, to Allah we are turning in desire.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 59]. He did not say "and to His Messenger," but made the desire directed to Him alone.

As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you are free, then strive, and to your Lord direct your longing.﴾

So desire, reliance, turning in repentance, and sufficiency are for Allah alone, just as worship, piety, and prostration are for Allah alone.

(Section)

As for desire for Allah, seeking His Face, and longing for meeting Him, these are the capital of the servant and the foundation of his affairs, the support of his good life, the root of his happiness, success, bliss, and the coolness of his eyes.

For this He created, with it He commanded, and with it the Messengers were sent and the Books revealed. The heart has no soundness and no bliss except by its desire being directed to Allah alone, so that He alone is its object of desire, its sought, and its aim, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when you are free, then strive, and to your Lord direct your longing.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger; indeed, to Allah we are turning in desire."﴾

Those who desire are of three types: one who desires Allah, one who desires what is with Allah, and one who turns away from Allah.

So the lover desires Him, the worker desires what is with Him, and the one content with this world instead of the Hereafter turns away from Him.

Whoever's desire is for Allah, Allah suffices him in every concern, takes charge of all his affairs, repels from him what he cannot repel from himself, and guards him as a mother guards her child, protecting him from all calamities.

Whoever prefers Allah over others, Allah prefers him over others.

Whoever belongs to Allah, Allah belongs to him where he does not belong to himself. Whoever knows Allah, nothing is more beloved to him than Him, and no desire remains in him for anything other than what brings him closer to Him and helps him on his journey to Him.

Among the signs of knowledge is awe: the more the servant's knowledge of his Lord grows, the more his awe and fear of Him grow, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.﴾
